# ROCm vLLM serving validation campaign on AMD Instinct hardware

## Description

Run a functional and performance validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving of
the supported model set on physical AMD Instinct accelerators. The campaign
produces the first-hand parity data the platform currently lacks and the
go/no-go scope (the validated model list) that determines what gets
productized. This is an Investigation: its outcome decides the scope of the
downstream serving-runtime productization work.

## Scope

- Run the campaign on dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procured or partner-lab —
  access is an open organizational precondition) provisioned with the ROCm
  driver stack and AMD GPU device plugin so that `amd.com/gpu` resources are
  allocatable. Node-stack provisioning is owned by the Platform Operator
  provisioning work this epic depends on; no AMD hardware exists in the CI
  fleet today.
- Exercise vLLM ROCm builds for each model in the supported model set on the
  AMD nodes, deployed through the existing ServingRuntime / InferenceService
  machinery.
- Collect functional pass/fail results and performance measurements
  (throughput, latency) per model against the CUDA baseline.
- Produce the go/no-go report: the validated model list (models cleared for
  productization), parity thresholds used, and root causes for any failures or
  parity gaps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The campaign runs on AMD Instinct nodes with the ROCm driver stack
  installed and `amd.com/gpu` resources discoverable by the scheduler
  (provided by the node-stack provisioning work this epic depends on).
- Every model in the supported model set has recorded functional pass/fail
  results and performance measurements on ROCm, alongside the CUDA baseline.
- Parity thresholds and go/no-go criteria are documented and agreed with
  stakeholders before the campaign concludes.
- A go/no-go report identifies the validated model list and any parity gaps,
  giving productization a definitive scope.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — full coverage: the validation campaign on physical AMD
  Instinct hardware establishing functional and performance parity data for
  vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for
  productization.

## Open Questions / Risks Carried by This Epic

- Hardware access (procurement vs partner-lab) is unresolved and is a
  precondition for starting; it is an organizational decision, not technical
  work.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and upstream
  communities and may constrain which vLLM ROCm builds the campaign can test.

# Konflux build pipeline for the vLLM ROCm runtime image

## Description

Onboard the vLLM ROCm runtime container image build to Konflux so the ROCm
variant of the default GenAI serving runtime is built and released through the
same pipeline machinery as the existing CUDA runtime builds. This is known-
recipe onboarding work in an existing, already-onboarded midstream repo — no
repo creation or license re-validation is needed.

## Scope

- Konflux application and pipeline configuration for the ROCm vLLM image build
  in the existing opendatahub-io midstream vLLM repo (new image variant in an
  existing repo; the CUDA build pipeline is the reference recipe).
- Build and release flow for the ROCm image matching the existing runtime
  release machinery, so the image can be pinned and shipped per platform
  version.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux pipeline builds the ROCm vLLM image successfully (green) on
  merge.
- The ROCm image flows through the same release process as the existing CUDA
  runtime images, with a pinnable digest per platform version.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — enabling coverage: provides the build pipeline for the
  productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime. Runs in parallel with the runtime
  productization work; the pipeline-green criterion gates its first release,
  not its start.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

Productize a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by the
validation campaign: a shippable ROCm runtime image and the ServingRuntime
definition that requests AMD GPU resources, deployable under KServe
InferenceServices. Today only CUDA (NVIDIA) builds of the vLLM runtime are
productized; ROCm builds exist upstream but are neither shipped nor supported.

## Scope

- ROCm vLLM runtime image as a new image variant in the existing midstream
  vLLM repo, built and released through the Konflux pipeline stood up for it.
- ServingRuntime / ClusterServingRuntime definition for the ROCm runtime
  requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources, mirroring the existing CUDA runtime
  definitions.
- Support scope limited to the models on the validated model list produced by
  the validation campaign; models not cleared are explicitly unsupported.
- End-to-end validation through KServe InferenceServices (KServe itself needs
  no code changes — it deploys runtimes accelerator-agnostically).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Support scope matches the validated model list from the validation campaign
  (go/no-go outcome); models outside the cleared list are documented as
  unsupported.
- The ROCm runtime image is built and released via the Konflux pipeline —
  build pipeline green.
- A ServingRuntime requesting `amd.com/gpu` deploys under KServe
  InferenceServices on AMD GPU nodes and exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints
  serving a cleared model.
- If upstream ROCm image releases do not align with the release train, the
  image is built from source in the midstream repo instead of consumed from
  upstream (fallback, not a scope change).
- The ROCm runtime ships alongside, and does not alter, the existing CUDA
  runtimes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — full coverage: a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime
  productized for the models the validation campaign clears.

## Gate

Gated by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome. If the campaign clears
only a subset of the model set, productize only that subset; if no models
clear, productization of the ROCm serving runtime is dropped.

# PyTorch ROCm training support in the Training Operator

## Description

Support PyTorch training on ROCm for single- and multi-GPU jobs run through
the Training Operator: PyTorchJob custom resources whose workers request
`amd.com/gpu` resources and run ROCm PyTorch images, admitted through Kueue
like their CUDA counterparts.

## Scope

- Enable and validate PyTorchJob worker pods requesting `amd.com/gpu` with
  ROCm PyTorch builds (published by PyTorch upstream), for single-GPU and
  multi-GPU (multi-worker) topologies.
- Validate on AMD Instinct nodes with the ROCm driver stack and device plugin
  in place (provided by the AMD GPU node-stack provisioning work this epic
  depends on).
- Coordinate queue admission behavior with the amd.com/gpu quota handling in
  the Distributed Workloads queueing stack (a runtime configuration concern —
  jobs must be admitted through Kueue with quota correctly accounted).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob running a ROCm PyTorch image completes training
  successfully on AMD GPU nodes.
- A multi-GPU (multi-worker) PyTorchJob completes on AMD GPU nodes.
- Jobs are admitted through Kueue with gang semantics intact when
  `amd.com/gpu` quota is available in the target ClusterQueue.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** — training half: PyTorch training on ROCm supported for
  single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm jobs

## Description

amd.com/gpu quota handling in the Distributed Workloads queueing stack so that
ROCm training jobs requesting AMD GPUs are admitted with correct quota
accounting, alongside the existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling.

## Scope

- ClusterQueue / LocalQueue quota configuration for `amd.com/gpu` resources in
  the Kueue quota model.
- Validation that quota accounting and all-or-nothing admission
  (waitForPodsReady) behave correctly for workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu`,
  including multi-GPU gang admission of PyTorchJobs, on AMD GPU nodes
  provisioned with the ROCm driver stack and device plugin (provided by the
  AMD GPU node-stack provisioning work this epic depends on).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ClusterQueue with `amd.com/gpu` quota admits multi-GPU PyTorchJobs with
  correct quota accounting.
- When `amd.com/gpu` quota is exhausted, further jobs queue (are not admitted)
  rather than partially starting.
- Quota for `amd.com/gpu` and `nvidia.com/gpu` is accounted independently —
  no cross-accelerator mis-accounting.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** — quota half: PyTorch ROCm jobs admitted through Kueue with
  amd.com/gpu quota handling.

# AMD GPU node-stack provisioning (ROCm driver, device plugin, resource discovery)

## Description

Provision the AMD GPU node stack — ROCm driver stack, AMD GPU device plugin,
and accelerator resource discovery — on AMD Instinct nodes so that
`amd.com/gpu` resources are allocatable by the scheduler. The platform
inventory has no AMD GPU node stack today: architecture context shows
accelerator discovery depends on the NVIDIA GPU Operator only, and no AMD
driver or device plugin is a platform component. Every epic that runs or
admits workloads on AMD GPUs (the vLLM serving validation campaign, PyTorch
ROCm training, and amd.com/gpu quota admission) needs this infrastructure in
place first. Provisioning is separated from the validation campaign per the
infrastructure-not-in-platform-inventory rule, so that all consumers depend
on it directly instead of on another team's investigation.

## Scope

- Install and verify the ROCm driver stack on AMD Instinct node(s), matching
  driver versions to the ROCm builds consumed by the serving and training
  images.
- Deploy the AMD GPU device plugin and verify `amd.com/gpu` resource
  discoverability and allocatability by the scheduler.
- Record the node-stack bring-up procedure (driver installation, device
  plugin deployment, version pinning) as repeatable configuration for
  re-provisioning on additional nodes or clusters.
- Hardware access itself (procurement vs partner-lab) is an unresolved
  organizational precondition, not technical work — provisioning starts once
  node access is secured.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AMD Instinct node(s) are available with the ROCm driver stack installed and
  version-pinned to match the ROCm builds under validation.
- The AMD GPU device plugin is running and `amd.com/gpu` resources are
  discoverable and allocatable by the scheduler on those nodes.
- The bring-up procedure is documented so the stack can be re-provisioned on
  additional nodes or clusters without rediscovery.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0), HLR-3 (P1)** — enabling coverage: provides the AMD GPU node
  infrastructure that the validation campaign (HLR-1) and the ROCm training
  and quota work (HLR-3) execute on. Priority P0 is inherited from the P0
  validation campaign it transitively enables.
